findings.claim: D-390 requires exactly one result per lookup, but the unconditional wording of several items overlaps with no precedence: an unknown method token or TRACE/CONNECT to a path that matches no route is both no-match (D-060, 404) and unsupported-method (D-066/D-067, 501); OPTIONS to a path that matches no route is both no-match (D-060) and automatic OPTIONS (D-064, 'a path without an explicit OPTIONS registration'); a POST, HEAD or OPTIONS without Upgrade (or with a non-websocket Upgrade value) to a WebSocket-only path is both WebSocket-only (D-069, 'a request without Upgrade', any method) and method-mismatch (D-061) or automatic OPTIONS (D-064). Two workers would pick different orders and the T02/T05/T06 statuses would differ.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one resolution order to the router contract, e.g. unsupported method (501) first, then path match (no-match 404 for every method including OPTIONS), then WebSocket-only only for GET/HEAD without an Upgrade: websocket header (other methods on a WS-only path get method-mismatch with Allow: GET), then explicit registration, automatic HEAD, automatic OPTIONS, method-mismatch; and assert each overlap in a router test.

findings.claim: Priority (D-054/D-055) is not stated as per-method or per-path. With GET /users/me and DELETE /users/:id, a DELETE /users/me either falls through to /users/:id (priority chosen among patterns registered for the request method, Express behaviour) or yields method-mismatch because the winning pattern /users/me has no DELETE. The Allow set of D-061 likewise is undefined as the winning pattern's methods or the union over every matching pattern. This changes T04 and T02/T06 outcomes.
findings.suggested_fix: State that priority is applied among patterns that have a registration for the request method (falling back to the next matching pattern), and that the method-mismatch Allow set is the union of methods over every pattern matching the path; add a router test for this case.

findings.claim: D-052 requires rejection 'with 400 before routing on every adapter', but wave 2 has no adapter, no dispatcher and no response: the dispatcher and in-memory adapter are wave 3 (D-394, D-108), the TinyHttpd adapter is wave 5, and the two-adapter parity test is I-021. Unlike D-056/D-058/D-069, D-052 carries no delegation note, so the wave 2 worker cannot implement it as written or may build out-of-scope adapter code.
findings.suggested_fix: Scope D-052 in wave 2 to an engine-free path decoder/validator in NaruServe-api that returns a rejection for every listed case (unit-tested against the TinyHttpd PercentCodec.decodePath rules and the request-line byte checks), with the 400 mapping owned by the wave 3 dispatcher and the cross-adapter assertion by I-021.

findings.claim: D-070 says wave 2 removes the (미확정) markers for the //, trailing-slash, case and TRACE/CONNECT policies in docs/api/routing.md, but those two markers read '설정 API (미확정)', i.e. the RestApp API names, which D-398 assigns to wave 3. Wave 2 cannot remove them without inventing the names (CLAUDE.md forbids naming what is undecided), so D-070 and D-398 contradict on who removes the markers.
findings.suggested_fix: Have wave 2 document the decided semantics in routing.md and leave the '설정 API (미확정)' name markers for wave 3 (D-398) to remove.

findings.claim: A successful WebSocket match (D-068) must be returned as the 'matched' variant, since D-390 lists exactly six variants and none is a WebSocket match, yet the matched variant carries only handler, params, actual method and auto-HEAD flag. With one opaque handler type parameter (D-389) the dispatcher cannot tell an app.ws registration from a GET registration, so wave 7 would have to change the router result or its type parameters, contradicting D-391 ('without changing the router').
findings.suggested_fix: Fix the contract in wave 2: either the matched result carries a WebSocket flag (or a WebSocket-matched variant), or the router stores WebSocket registrations with their own opaque type parameter; test that a WS match is distinguishable from a GET match on the same path.

findings.claim: D-067 correctly records that TinyHttpd answers CONNECT with an authority-form target with 501 before dispatch and rewrites absolute-form targets to origin-form, but wave 3's D-442 requires any raw path not starting with '/' to get 400 identically on the in-memory and TinyHttpd adapters, which TinyHttpd cannot do for CONNECT host:port (501) and does differently for absolute-form (routed as origin-form).
findings.suggested_fix: Exempt CONNECT authority-form (501, the D-020 deferred gap) and absolute-form targets from the D-442 identical-400 rule, or have the in-memory adapter mirror TinyHttpd's request-target handling.

findings.claim: Pattern validation covers only Express wildcard/regex syntax; a pattern repeating a variable name (/a/:id/:id) or with an empty name (/a/:) is not addressed, so req.param would be ambiguous.
findings.suggested_fix: Make duplicate or empty variable names a configuration error at registration, with a router test.

findings.claim: D-038 delegates the MethodSet membership/iteration accessor names to #2 (this wave), but D-070, the wave open-items list, names only the routing policy semantics, and docs/api/routing.md documents no MethodSet accessor nor marks one (미확정). The worker may pick names without a recorded decision or the required docs/api update (CLAUDE.md: API changes update docs/api).
findings.suggested_fix: Extend D-070 (or the wave SDS) to record the chosen MethodSet accessor names (e.g. membership and iteration) and add them to docs/api/routing.md with Java/Kotlin examples.
